gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a 120 V-only generator or shore feed can't charge any of the low-frequency 24 V split-phase units it named. Sun Gold says its 4000 W and 6000 W 24 V units 'require 240VAC input', and Sigineer and AIMS chargers take only 240 V across L1–L2. Sigineer gives a 160–264 Vac input window, so a 120 V source is below the 160 V minimum.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Sigineer 6000 W page, the Sigineer 3000 W page, the ecosolarkits split-phase guide, liveoffthegrid.com/specs/inverters and our own dealectric.com/best-split-phase-inverter. The cited Sigineer page has the raw spec ('accepts 240 volts AC… 160-264Vac', 'only L1, L2, and ground are required'), but it doesn't say what that means for a 120 V generator. Ecosolarkits says 'needs a 240V AC input (not 120V)' only about a 48 V Sungold 15 kW unit, and it says its 24 V models are sold out. Liveoffthegrid marks 'Gen in' as yes or no with no voltage and lists no 24 V units. Our page covers only 48 V hybrids and doesn't mention AC input. ChatGPT's answer leaves the input requirement out completely, even though three of its four cards (Sun Gold 6000 W, Sun Gold 4000 W, AIMS 6000 W) are 240 V-input units.
decides: This works as a gate before any pick. If the shopper's backup or charging source is a 120 V-only generator or a 120 V shore or RV plug, the Sun Gold, AIMS and Sigineer 24 V split-phase units won't charge from it or pass it through. The shopper then needs a generator with a 240 V outlet, or a step-up autotransformer. If the shopper already has 240 V from a generator or the grid, any of them works. Choose by per-leg limit next: Sigineer 6000 W allows 3,000 W per 120 V leg and 100% imbalance. After that, choose by listing: AIMS 4000 W cites UL 458/1741/1012, while the Sigineer pages list no certification.
